title: Deferred residency credits and transparent chunk migration for KV paged cache
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: As multi-tenant workloads run longer sequences and varied prompt patterns, the paged KV cache exhibits oscillating residency: hot chunks become temporarily evicted by short-lived spikes, causing decode stalls and repeated prefill work. Current eviction heuristics overreact to instantaneous touch frequency and do not account for near-term reuse or tenant priority.

Proposal: Implement a two-part system: (1) residency credits (a deferred-crediting scheme) that accrues soft-residency for recently used chunks and decays on a configurable half-life; and (2) transparent background chunk migration that consolidates low-value fragments into contiguous chunks when bandwidth/idle cycles allow. The residency credits act as soft-leases to resist premature eviction during brief pressure spikes, while chunk migration reduces fragmentation and improves contiguous kernel fetch efficiency.

Goals:
- Reduce decode latency tail for sequences that would otherwise trigger repeat prefill of recently-used KV regions.
- Lower token compute overhead by avoiding unnecessary prefill work during transient pressure.
- Reduce fragmentation over time to improve kernel read efficiency and decrease GPU memory churn.

Acceptance criteria:
- 90th percentile decode latency improves by >= 10% for mixed tenant workload in the benchmark harness.
- Total prefill token cost per 1k requests decreases by >= 12% in steady-state mixed traffic.
- Background migration overhead (measured as additional cycles used for consolidation) remains < 5% of GPU time under normal load.

Design summary:
- Residency credits: each KV chunk gets a numeric credit value when touched; credits are topped up for repeated access and decay exponentially with a configurable half-life (e.g., 30s). Eviction picks consider credit weight in addition to LRU recency and chunk size. Credits are tenant-scoped so high-priority tenants can be given higher base credit multipliers.
- Deferred eviction window: when eviction pressure occurs, chunks below a soft-credit threshold are eligible; chunks with credits in a small deferred window (e.g., last 3s) are skipped unless pressure persists beyond a hard-threshold. This prevents thrash during brief peaks.
- Transparent chunk migration: a background worker consolidates partially-filled pages into contiguous chunks when the device has spare cycles or during low-utilization periods; migration is single-shot per chunk and uses cooperative copy with preemption hooks. The worker prioritizes consolidation that reduces kernel scatter/gather length for recent access patterns.
- Backpressure integration: the scheduler exposes a tenant-level pressure signal that informs admission and batching decisions; if global pressure exceeds tiers, credits can be temporarily ignored for low-priority tenants to preserve SLAs.

Trade-offs considered:
- Holding soft-residency longer increases memory occupation; mitigated by tunable half-life and global caps.
- Background migration consumes cycles that could add slight latency if run too aggressively; solution is conservative default and adaptive backoff based on observed tail latency.
- Complexity added to eviction policy increases scheduler surface area — we keep the API internal and provide observability to iterate safely.

Observability and metrics to add:
- credit_accrual_rate, credit_decay_events, eviction_via_credit_bypass, background_migration_ops, migration_bytes_moved, prefill_repeat_rate_per_chunk, tenant_pressure_score.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout, start with internal canary (redwood-internal), then opt-in for Dedicated customers, monitor metrics for two weeks, then enable default for hosted small-tier.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Kickoff: Feasibility spike completed. Prototype of credit accrual in go runtime + unit tests for decay timer. Observed a 6% reduction in 95th pct decode in microbenchmarks.

2025-02-20 - Design review: PM (Lina Gomez) and Infra (Ravi Singh) approved the soft-lease concept. Concern: migration IO could interfere with scheduled batch windows; added preemption hook requirement.

2025-02-26 - Implementation: Chunk credit bookkeeping implemented in C++ runtime; credits stored as 16-bit fixed-point to limit memory overhead. Experimental flag added: runtime.features.residency_credits.

2025-03-01 - Integration test: End-to-end harness shows prefill_repeat_rate_per_chunk dropped 18% for our multi-tenant trace. Background migration still prototype; we observed 0.9% extra GPU time under synthetic load.

2025-03-04 - Code review: Feedback from reviewer (Maya Chen) to add tenant-bucket smoothing to avoid starvation; action item created to tune decay half-life per workload. PR #4821 ready for internal merge after one refactor.
Follow-ups: add adaptive half-life controller (future ticket), add knob for tenant credit multiplier in console, add migration failure retry and telemetry.
